arxiv-2101-03061.creator: Csenge Lili Ködmön and Zsolt Lángi
arxiv-2101-03061.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Csenge Lili Ködmön and Zsolt Lángi. A convex polygon Q Q is inscribed in a convex polygon P P if every side of P P contains at least one vertex of Q Q . We present algorithms for finding a minimum area and a minimum perimeter convex polygon inscribed in any given convex n n -gon in O ⁡ ( n ) O(n) and O ⁡ ( n 3 ) O(n^{3}) time, respectively. We also investigate other variants of this problem.

arxiv-2207-12642.title: Euclidean Dynamical Triangulations Revisited
arxiv-2207-12642.creator: Muhammad Asaduzzaman, Simon Catterall
arxiv-2207-12642.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Muhammad Asaduzzaman, Simon Catterall. We conduct numerical simulations of a model of four dimensional quantum gravity in which the path integral over continuum Euclidean metrics is approximated by a sum over combinatorial triangulations. At fixed volume the model contains a discrete Einstein-Hilbert term with coupling κ \kappa and local measure term with coupling β \beta that weights triangulations according to the number of simplices sharing each vertex.

Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are extremely strong radio flares lasting several micro to milliseconds and come from unidentified objects at cosmological distances, most of which are only seen once.

arxiv-2305-07801.title: Quantum learning machines.
arxiv-2305-07801.creator: Gerard Milburn
arxiv-2305-07801.description: Abstract Physical learning machines, be they classical or quantum, are necessarily dissipative systems. The rate of energy dissipation decreases as the learning error rate decreases linking thermodynamic efficiency and learning efficiency. In the classical case the energy is dissipated as heat. We give an example based on a quantum optical perceptron where the energy is dissipated as spontaneous emission.

arxiv-2310-13781.title: How Much Consistency Is Your Accuracy Worth?
arxiv-2310-13781.creator: Jacob K. Johnson, Ana Marasović
arxiv-2310-13781.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Jacob K. Johnson, Ana Marasović. Contrast set consistency is a robustness measurement that evaluates the rate at which a model correctly responds to all instances in a bundle of minimally different examples relying on the same knowledge. To draw additional insights, we propose to complement consistency with relative consistency — the probability that an equally accurate model would surpass the consistency of the proposed model, given a distribution over possible consistencies. Models with 100% relative consistency have reached a consistency peak for their accuracy.

arxiv-2311-02197.title: Absence of localization in weakly interacting Floquet circuits
arxiv-2311-02197.creator: Dominik Hahn, Luis Colmenarez
arxiv-2311-02197.description: Abstract We present a family of Floquet circuits that can interpolate between non-interacting qubits, free propagation, generic interacting, and dual-unitary dynamics. We identify the operator entanglement entropy of the two-qubit gate as a good quantitative measure of the interaction strength.

arxiv-2410-22085.title: Robust high-dimensional Gaussian and bootstrap approximations for trimmed sample means
arxiv-2410-22085.creator: Lucas Resende
arxiv-2410-22085.description: Abstract Robust mean estimation has largely focused on concentration guarantees under heavy tails and contamination. We study robustness from a different perspective: high-dimensional Gaussian and bootstrap approximations. We show that trimmed sample means admit Gaussian and bootstrap approximations under finite (p)-th moment assumptions, even in high-dimensional regimes and in the presence of adversarial contamination.

arxiv-2411-10603.title: A Novel MLLM-based Approach for Autonomous Driving in Different Weather Conditions PubID: pubid: 0000–0000/00$00.00 © 2021 IEEE
arxiv-2411-10603.creator: Sonda Fourati, Wael Jaafar, Noura Baccar
arxiv-2411-10603.description: Abstract Autonomous driving (AD) technology promises to revolutionize daily transportation by making it safer, more efficient, and more comfortable. Their role in reducing traffic accidents and improving mobility will be vital to the future of intelligent transportation systems. Autonomous driving in harsh environmental conditions presents significant challenges that demand robust and adaptive solutions and require more investigation.

arxiv-2502-19292.title: Optimal COVID-19 Vaccine Prioritization by Age Depends Critically on Inter-group Contacts and Vaccination Rates
arxiv-2502-19292.creator: Iker Atienza-Diez, Gabriel Rodriguez-Maroto, Saúl Ares, Susanna Manrubia
arxiv-2502-19292.description: Abstract The limited availability of COVID-19 vaccines has prompted extensive research on optimal vaccination strategies. Previous studies have considered various non-pharmaceutical interventions, vaccine efficacy, and distribution strategies. In this work, we address the combined effects of inter-group contacts and vaccination rates under contact reduction, analyzing the Spanish population’s demographic and age group contact patterns and incorporating reinfection dynamics.

arxiv-2505-17873.title: MOOSE-Chem3: Toward Experiment-Guided Hypothesis Ranking via Simulated Experimental Feedback
arxiv-2505-17873.creator: Wanhao Liu *, Zonglin Yang *, Jue Wang, Lidong Bing, Di Zhang, Dongzhan Zhou, Yuqiang Li, Houqiang Li, Erik Cambria, Wanli Ouyang
arxiv-2505-17873.description: Abstract Hypothesis ranking is a crucial component of automated scientific discovery, particularly in natural sciences where wet-lab experiments are costly and throughput-limited . Existing approaches focus on pre-experiment ranking, relying solely on a language model’s internal reasoning without incorporating empirical outcomes. We introduce the task of experiment-guided ranking , which prioritizes hypotheses based on feedback from previously tested ones.

arxiv-2506-09525.title: Beyond Personalization: Federated Recommendation with Calibration via Low-rank Decomposition
arxiv-2506-09525.creator: Jundong Chen, Honglei Zhang, Haoxuan Li, Chunxu Zhang, Zhiwei Li, Yidong Li, Key Laboratory of Big Data & Artificial Intelligence in Transportation, Ministry of Education, Beijing Jiaotong University, Peking University, Jilin University, University of Technology Sydney jundongchen@bjtu.edu.cn , ydli
arxiv-2506-09525.description: Abstract Federated recommendation (FR) is a promising paradigm to protect user privacy in recommender systems. Distinct from general federated scenarios, FR inherently needs to preserve client-specific parameters, i.e. , user embeddings, for privacy and personalization. However, we empirically find that globally aggregated item embeddings can induce skew in user embeddings, resulting in suboptimal performance.

arxiv-2507-22075.title: Prototype-Guided Pseudo-Labeling with Neighborhood-Aware Consistency for Unsupervised Adaptation
arxiv-2507-22075.creator: Eman Ali, Chetan Arora, and Muhammad Haris Khan
arxiv-2507-22075.description: Abstract In unsupervised adaptation for vision-language models such as CLIP, pseudo-labels derived from zero-shot predictions often exhibit significant noise, particularly under domain shifts or in visually complex scenarios. Conventional pseudo-label filtering approaches, which rely on fixed confidence thresholds, tend to be unreliable in fully unsupervised settings.

pmc-13195224.title: Adverse events associated with statin co-use in breast cancer patients: a disproportionality analysis based on the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System
pmc-13195224.creator: Yunnan Zhang, Wenxing Peng, Wei Yang, Yang Gao, Yannan Fan, Qianqian Guo
pmc-13195224.description: Background:An increasing number of breast cancer patients are using statins concomitantly. However, there are relatively few safety studies on the association between statins and adverse events (AEs) during breast cancer treatment.Objective:This study aims to systematically evaluate the disproportionality signals associated with statin use and the reporting of AEs across different system organ classes (SOCs) in breast cancer patients.

pmc-13583911.title: The Impact of Environmental, Nutritional, and Animal Welfare Labeling of Plant‐Based Cream Cheese on Consumer Perception
pmc-13583911.creator: Cayla E J Weiler, Chase D Morhart, Brianna Power, Zach Adams, Matthew B McSweeney
pmc-13583911.description: Plant‐based alternatives (PBAs) to dairy products are increasingly positioned as nutritionally beneficial, sustainable, and ethical food choices; however, consumer acceptance of PBAs remains limited, partly due to sensory challenges and uncertainty surrounding effective product communication strategies. This study investigated the influence of environmental, nutritional, and animal welfare labeling on consumer perception of plant‐based cream cheese (PBCC).
